title: Borne on the Wings of Light
description: Borne on the Wings of Light in Tonic Solfa to ST. JOHN (PARISH CHOIR), doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: John Brownlie translated these words from the Greek service books for Hymns from the Morningland (Paisley, 1911).
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Hallelujah Metre (6.6.6.6.8.8), and this page sets them to ST. JOHN (PARISH CHOIR); any other Hallelujah Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Borne on the wings of light, Be-hold the Lord as-cend, Up to the por-tals bright Where heav-enly powers at-tend, And fling the gates of glo-ry wide, While prais-es rise like flow-ing tide.

lines: Borne on the wings of light,
And fling the gates of glory wide,
While praises rise like flowing tide.
Loud plaudits hail the Victor now,
Who comes with triumph on His brow.
Lord, in the peace of heaven,
Far from our toil and pain,
That brought Thee to Thy blest abode.
And see the toils we bear,
And hear the prayers we send;
We need not languish in the night,
Though heaven receive Thee from our sight.
Who fought with us in earthly strife,
And won for us immortal life.

source: John Brownlie, Hymns from the Morningland (1911)
licence: Public domain: John Brownlie died in 1925.
credits: Translated by John Brownlie (1857–1925) from the Greek, public domain, as printed in Hymns from the Morningland; set to ST. JOHN (PARISH CHOIR) by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
